issues.issue: The plan says pinned instances (SiteMini on shelf and dock cards, the PickFlight clone) 'read SAVED only'. In the code, saved means world.siteEdits, and that belongs to the CURRENT site. SiteMini takes no site id, and SitePreview always reads the current world. Once a second live site exists (startBuild creates a 'live' row, and block M builds one), every live card on the shelf and the dock shows the edits of whichever site is open. fit-ration's card loses its saved edits while you stand in the new site. The PickFlight clone of target site B renders the LEAVING site A's edits in flight, then set({site:B}) swaps the text underneath it when it lands. That is exactly the seam SiteMini was built to remove. The planned block-O test 'site switch does not leak' reads only localStorage, so it would pass while the pixels leak.
issues.evidence: prototype/src/modules/sites/SiteMini.tsx:30,52 (no site prop; <SitePreview path="/"/>); prototype/src/modules/preview/SitePreview.tsx:271-279 (useWorld reads the current brief/planEdits; siteEdits would follow the same pattern); prototype/src/modules/sites/SitesShelf.tsx:337 (every live card uses SiteMini), :419 (the flight clone renders SitePreview from the current world), :144-153 (land() calls set({site}) only on landing); prototype/src/modules/home/Dock.tsx:609; prototype/src/modules/chat/send.ts:771 (new rows are thumb:'live'); SiteMini.tsx:5-10 (the no-seam rationale). The same latent bug exists today for footer page lists (brief/planEdits), but it is invisible because the footer sits below the card's crop; a hero-title edit is at the top of the card.
issues.fix: Give SitePreview an explicit content source. Either a `site` prop, or `slice?: Pick<World,'brief'|'planEdits'|'siteEdits'>` resolved by a selector siteSliceOf(world,id) = id===world.site ? world : world.stash[id] ?? SITE_SLICES[id]. SiteMini/SiteCard/Dock pass project.id; PickFlight passes the TARGET project's slice. Only the canvas instance (no pinned path, current site) layers ui.editDraft on top. Block O must assert pixels as well: innerText of `[data-site-card=<other live id>] [data-site-mini] h1` stays unchanged after editing the open site, and the flight clone's h1 equals the landed canvas h1.

issues.issue: PhotoRef {kind:'upload', src: data URL} puts image bytes into World. syncUrl JSON.stringifies the whole world and writes it to localStorage synchronously on EVERY world.set(): each chat send (at the bubble-spring start), every build beat, every console click. The bytes are also duplicated in the stash, because set() leaves a stale stash[currentSite] entry after a restore. The plan names the quota but understates it. Once setItem throws, syncUrl swallows the error and the ENTIRE world stops persisting (transcript, publish state, purchases), not just the photo.
issues.evidence: prototype/src/state/world.ts:1014-1019 (syncUrl stringify + setItem, errors ignored), :1083-1085 (called on every set), :1036-1038 (stash keeps the restored site's old entry); send.ts:103 (build beat set), :145 (send set). Probe in this container (headless Chromium 1194, 30.09.2026, scratchpad undo-probe/probe4.mjs): a world with 3×200 KB photos plus 2 stash copies (1.76 MB JSON) costs 38-45 ms per set versus 0.1 ms for today's world, and 3.5 MB more throws QuotaExceededError. Status: verified (probe; absolute ms will differ on the designer's machine). The springs are deliberately main-thread (onUpdate stubs), so a 40 ms stall drops frames in exactly the animations the project protects.
issues.fix: Keep the bytes out of World. Store uploads under their own key (e.g. 'remixer-prototype/media/v1/<id>', or IndexedDB), written once on Save, with World holding only {kind:'upload', id, name}. Downscale before storing (the plan's ~800 px). On quota failure show an explicit error in the Replace window, and never write inside world.set. Alternatively, and more simply for a prototype, make uploads session-only (object in module memory) and ask the designer whether a reload must keep them (already question 10). Add a block-O check that a set() after an upload stays under a few ms (measure performance.now around a console toggle).

issues.issue: The plan leaves native undo alone ('while the caret is in the text, ⌘Z undoes the typed letters as usual; we do not intercept ⌘Z in the chat'). Chromium's undo stack is shared per document across editing hosts. Native ⌘Z in one host walks into previously edited hosts. ⌘Z in the chat composer textarea, after its own history runs out, reverts committed site text. ⌘Z with nothing focused does the same. In all these cases the DOM changes and the draft/store does not. Because React does not own the text and the imperative write only runs when the value differs, nothing repaints it back, so Save persists a text the screen no longer shows.
issues.evidence: Probe (Chromium 1194, 30.09.2026, scratchpad undo-probe/probe.mjs): case1 — typed in A, then B, Ctrl+Z twice in B → B reverted, then focus jumped to A and A reverted; case2 — typed in site host A, then in a textarea, Ctrl+Z twice in the textarea → the textarea reverted, then A reverted; case3 — blur everything, Ctrl+Z → A reverted. probe2/probe3: preventDefault on the keydown stops it; rewriting el.textContent (even to the same value) on commit makes the stale native step inert; removing contenteditable on Exit also makes it inert. Status: verified (probe). Composer is a <textarea> (ChatPanel.tsx:1022). PlanEditable writes only when the value differs (PlanEditable.tsx:49-54).
issues.fix: On every commit (blur/Enter), rewrite the host's textContent imperatively even when it is equal: this retires the browser's steps for that host. While the session is open, add a capture-phase keydown handler: ⌘Z/⇧⌘Z/Ctrl+Y outside a focused site host → preventDefault and route to the session stack. Inside a focused host, first ⌘Z → restore the value at focus time (Esc semantics), next ⌘Z → session stack. Decide the composer explicitly (see the composer issue). Add a block-O probe: edit a heading, focus the composer, type, press ⌘Z ×3, and assert that the heading's innerText still equals the stored draft.

issues.issue: The leave guard 'Save your edits? [Save] [Discard]' is specified as useConfirm.ask. ConfirmDialog cannot express that. ConfirmRequest has only onConfirm, and the cancel button, Esc and scrim all just close() without a callback. So 'Discard and continue to the shelf/Domains/Publish' is impossible, and dismissing the dialog cannot be told apart from Discard. The dialog also autofocuses Cancel, which would be Discard, so Enter would throw the edits away.
issues.evidence: prototype/src/ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx:47-58 (interface: confirmLabel, cancelLabel, tone, onConfirm only), :80 (Escape → close()), :86 (focus goes to Cancel), :99 (scrim mousedown → close()), :118-121 (cancel onClick={close}). The shared component's first caller is Unlink in PublishPanel.
issues.fix: Extend ConfirmRequest with optional onCancel plus an explicit dismiss outcome, or add a small three-way variant: [Keep editing] (default focus, Esc and scrim) · [Discard] · [Save]. Leave Unlink's behaviour byte-identical. Put the guard INSIDE the ui actions (openSurface, openDomains, goHome, togglePublish(true), and the shelf opener) so one wrapper covers every entry point instead of sprinkling guards over the rail, header, Home and Publish.

issues.issue: The plan says saved edits survive reload only 'sometimes'. In practice they NEVER survive F5 in dev or vite preview, which is where check:brief and local demos run. Save sets unpublished+1, so syncUrl writes ?u=1. On reload the URL branch wins whole over DEFAULT_WORLD and rescues only a resumable transcript. The world comes back with u=1 ('1 unpublished change') and no edit at all, which is an inconsistent state rather than just a lost edit.
issues.evidence: prototype/src/state/world.ts:883 (non-default axes go into the query; DEFAULT unpublished 0 at :617), :982-1007 (URL wins; only sent is rescued, and only when chat==='working'), :1014-1017 (replaceState on every set). In the published artifact the sandbox may block replaceState (comment at world.ts:1011-1013), so the artifact and preview behave differently. Status: code-fact, 30.09.2026.
issues.fix: Treat a URL that equals worldToParams(saved) as a reload of our own state and restore the snapshot whole. That one rule also fixes the loss of planEdits, stash, cart and sent on F5. Test URLs always include p=built, which syncUrl never writes (it is the default), so existing blocks are unaffected. If the designer prefers the status quo, block O's reload check must use a clean URL, and the risk text must say 'always in preview', not 'sometimes'.

issues.issue: The hover model '.site-stage[data-editing] [data-edit]:hover ring, opacity only' breaks on this DOM, and the selection overlay's mechanics are unspecified. A pseudo-element ring on a meal photo is clipped by the card's overflow-hidden (the tile is flush with the card edge). CSS :hover also matches every [data-edit] ancestor, so nested editables light together. Reusing the plan editor's .plan-edit trick (margin -8/padding 8) would reflow the max-w-[16ch] hero title. A JS-positioned selection ring goes stale during the 340 ms device animation, which changes width/height per frame, and during a chat-resizer drag, which writes --chat-w outside React. AnimatePresence keeps the exiting page in the DOM with the same keys (nav/footer are shared), so querySelector('[data-edit=…]') can hit the dying page after a cross-page undo. A permanently promoted overlay layer once cost the suite's frame floor.
issues.evidence: SitePreview.tsx:72-73 (overflow-hidden rounded card with a flush photo tile), :26 (sticky z-10 nav with backdrop-blur), :44 (h1 mx-auto max-w-[16ch]), :284-306 (page keyed by path, nav+footer rendered on every page); index.css:4489-4497 (.plan-edit margin/padding); App.tsx:1270-1278 (stage animates width/height for 0.34 s); App.tsx:1252-1257 ('a second permanently promoted full-canvas layer cost the software rasteriser a frame floor (the suite's 8-samples-in-300-ms floor read 7)'); CLAUDE.md, ChatResizer section (drag bypasses React).
issues.fix: Keep data-edit on LEAF nodes only, never nested. Draw hover and selection with ONE overlay element mounted only in edit mode, INSIDE the page's scroll content (make the flex min-h-full wrapper relative, inside the keyed page motion.div). Then it scrolls natively with no scroll listener, is not clipped by cards, and leaves with its page. Move it on pointerover/pointerout (boundary crossings, not every pointermove) with a transform plus one rect read, and fade it with opacity. Re-measure through a ResizeObserver on the page content. Hide it while the device animation runs and on onAnimationComplete. Resolve targets inside `[data-site-page="${path}"]` only. No will-change on the overlay, and zero layout change to site elements (no padding/margin/position tricks).

issues.fix: Split keys per text run (e.g. home.stat.0.value / home.stat.0.label, contact.kitchen.value), and decide whether macros are editable as whole strings or not at all (designer question). Render buttons as non-editable in mode, or exclude them (page names are already excluded). issues.issue: Busy gating and the composer during a session. The entry gate includes `reloading`, and every site switch fires triggerReload for 2.2 s, so the pill would read 'Remixer is working' after every switch when nothing is working. The reverse gap is worse. With a CLEAN session open, a composer send is allowed. The glow then burns while ~40 contentEditable hosts are live, and the glow was measured at 4 fps, which makes typing unusable. Meanwhile the AI reply adds +1 and 'changes the site' under an open editing session.
issues.evidence: App.tsx:836 (busy = generating || chat working || reloading), App.tsx:826-834 (measured 4 fps with the glow versus 60 without); SitesShelf.tsx:82, 152 (SWITCH_GLOW_MS 2200 after every landing); send.ts:145, 242-253 (send → chat 'working' → +1).
issues.fix: Gate entry on `project==='generating' || chat==='working'` only, not on `reloading`. Pick one rule for the composer while in mode and ask the designer: either the composer is locked in mode with a hint, or a send closes the session first (Save/Discard if dirty). Either way the glow never runs while hosts are editable.

issues.issue: The session in ui has no owner. editDraft is an unkeyed layer, while forced world moves (a console preset, project≠'built', a site move) happen in the world store, which ui does not observe. The plan's 'forced paths discard silently' has no mechanism. `preset` identity cannot signal staging, because saveEdits itself calls set(..., preset) with the same name. A React effect would paint one frame of site A's draft over site B. Collapsing the preview by drag (previewOpen=false) is also missing from the auto-close list.
issues.evidence: world.ts:1024-1086 (set touches the world store only); send.ts:665-671 (editPlanText passes the current preset); ui.ts:579 (openSurface), 483-486 (goHome); ChatResizer.tsx:31 (PREVIEW_MIN collapse).
issues.fix: Put `site` into the session and ignore the draft whenever session.site ≠ world.site. Close through a module-level useWorld.subscribe (synchronous, no effect frame) when the site, project, or a preset application changes, and have ScenarioPanel's apply call closeEditor('discard') explicitly. Add previewOpen→false to the guard.

issues.issue: The plan justifies session-in-ui with 'flows.ts can call ui actions later for a CEO demo'. flows.ts was deleted, and CLAUDE.md forbids bringing it back or writing 'for the CEO demo' again. So the mode is simply not console-stageable, and the plan should say so rather than promise a flow.
issues.evidence: CLAUDE.md:235-241 ('ДВИЖКА ФЛОУ БОЛЬШЕ НЕТ… Не возвращать — и не писать «для демо CEO» заново'); `ls prototype/src/state` shows only scenarios.ts, ui.ts, world.ts; git 8d078e1 deleted flows.ts (697 lines).
issues.fix: Delete that line. If the designer wants 'editor open' stageable from the console, make only `editing: boolean` a world axis: toggles are rare, so the syncUrl cost is irrelevant, and it is not in the URL. Draft, selection and history stay in ui. Ask the designer; don't decide silently.

issues.issue: The state is not minimal and has type gaps. editDraft and editPast/editFuture are two writers of one truth, since the draft equals saved-at-open plus past, and they can drift. EditStep.before:null means 'original', but draft.photo is Record<key, PhotoRef> with no 'original' variant, so an undo back to the original photo cannot be written into the draft. PlanEditable commits on every blur, so reusing it pushes no-op steps: clicking in and out marks the session dirty, and Exit asks 'Save your edits?' for nothing.
issues.evidence: Draft state_model (ui: editDraft + editPast/editFuture; PhotoRef union); prototype/src/modules/chat/PlanEditable.tsx:82 (onBlur always calls onCommit).
issues.fix: Derive the draft with useMemo from a snapshot of siteEdits at open plus the past steps, or keep the draft and make commit/undo/redo its only writers. Add PhotoRef {kind:'original'} (or allow null in the draft) and derive dirty as !sameEdits(merge(saved,draft), saved). Push a step only when after ≠ before.

issues.issue: The storage bump is defensible but not mandated, and it does not fix the root cause. The designer's rule is 'bump when a DEFAULT changes'. Adding siteEdits changes no default, and `{...DEFAULT_WORLD, ...saved}` already fills the top level. The leak exists only because restore spreads an incomplete slice. A v7 bump retires the designer's demo world and leaves the same trap open for the next per-site axis.
issues.evidence: world.ts:1003 (`{...DEFAULT_WORLD, ...saved}`), :1037-1038 (`{...(restored ?? {}), ...patch, stash}`), :579-582 (SITE_BASE already typed as a complete slice minus 5 keys); user brief: 'Если меняется дефолт мира, подними версию ключа'.
issues.fix: Make restore complete: `{...SITE_FRESH, ...restored, ...patch, stash}` when restored ≠ null, where SITE_FRESH is one TypeScript-complete table of empties. That is generic, not a per-axis guard. Keep v7 only if the designer accepts losing his snapshot, and then update the 9 harness literals plus the scratchpad probes (site-switch/edges.mjs, site-switch/probe.mjs, pane-motions/trace.mjs, page-menu-board/probe.mjs) and CLAUDE.md.

issues.issue: Dishes already have a database in the prototype's fiction. Cloud's table IS the data behind the site: six meals with ids 'power-bowl'… and an image_url column. It duplicates SitePreview's MEALS constant, and the plan adds a third copy (content.ts). A VE edit of a meal name or photo would contradict the Cloud window. Lovable also treats data-driven text as non-inline-editable.
issues.evidence: prototype/src/data/cloud.ts:12-17 ('Cloud shows what is behind that page — so the table holds those six meals'), :43+ (rows with ids); SitePreview.tsx:257-264 (MEALS, no id); web research: Lovable 'Dynamic text cannot be edited' (docs.lovable.dev/features/preview-toolbar, verified via snippets, seen 30.09.2026).
issues.fix: Use one dish source: SitePreview reads cloud.ts rows and keys by their ids. Ask the designer whether meal cards are static copy (editable in VE, and Cloud mirrors the edit) or data (VE shows 'Edit in Cloud'). Don't create content.ts copies of the dishes.

issues.issue: The artifact trims fonts to glyphs found in the build plus printable ASCII and a curated tail. Characters a customer types into the site (é, ü, ñ, ß, curly quotes not in the tail) render in a system fallback mid-word in the PUBLISHED artifact only. check:brief runs on vite preview, where all glyphs are kept, so it cannot catch this.
issues.evidence: prototype/scripts/build-artifact.mjs:23-35 ('This trim is ARTIFACT-ONLY'), :61-72 (usedCharacters: 0x20-0x7e plus the curated tail plus build strings).
issues.fix: Add Latin-1 Supplement (U+00A0-00FF) to the curated tail for the site's face. It costs bytes against the ~1.1 KB headroom, so apply the rule: try the publish, then raise CEILING. Or document it as a known artifact limitation and tell the designer.

issues.issue: Frame-floor and harness-budget risks. Editable wrappers with refs and layout effects on every text node raise the mount cost of every page swap, every PickFlight clone and every mini. The /services page handoff is already one of the two known flaky timing checks. Any 'Visual Editor …' string that sits in the DOM before a site exists (a hidden tooltip, an 'Always free: Visual Editor edits' row) fails the pre-site check, because p.$('text=…') matches hidden nodes.
issues.evidence: User brief (the flaky /services handoff and Cloud rail tile); check-brief-flow.mjs:5378-5514 (page-swap filming), :1392-1393 (`!(await p.$('text=Visual Editor'))`); SitePreview.tsx:284-306.
issues.fix: Outside edit mode, render plain text with no wrappers or effects. Mount the overlay, handlers and data attributes only while editing, and switch once on entry (layout effect, no blink). Keep every new 'Visual Editor' string behind project==='built'. Block-O assertions should read world state, innerText and aria, not wait on springs.

issues.issue: Photo sources and size budget. 'Photos on your site' as a drawn set costs bytes against the 1,114-byte headroom and needs a scrolling grid. data: images are already proven in the published page through CSS masks (img-src covers CSS images), so only blob: is unproven, not data:.
issues.evidence: build-artifact.mjs:212 (CEILING 1,150,263 versus live v119 1,149,149); index.css:1933-1935, 2169-2181, 3691-3693 (data:image/svg+xml masks shipped in the artifact); CLAUDE.md ScrollArea rule.
issues.fix: Reuse the site's own tint+emoji tiles as the library (zero bytes; the same tiles cloud.ts already mirrors), and scroll the grid in ScrollArea. Use data: URLs, not blob:, for uploads, and still verify the upload flow in the claude.ai panel as the plan says.

issues.issue: Overrides have no language. Some site strings are bilingual through t() (footer 'Ready when you are.', the 404 copy), while siteEdits.text is a single string per key. What an EN edit shows under the UK locale is undefined.
issues.evidence: SitePreview.tsx:115, 231-233, 241 (t({en,uk})); src/i18n.ts (EN default, UK second); draft SiteEdits.text: Record<EditKey,string>.
issues.fix: State the rule: an override replaces the string in every locale, since it is the customer's site copy rather than builder chrome. Write it in the feature base and the decisions line.

missing_topics: How pinned SitePreview instances (shelf and dock cards, PickFlight clone) get THEIR site's saved slice from the stash instead of the current world
Where uploaded photo bytes live, outside the World object that syncUrl serializes on every set(), and what the quota-failure UI says
Interplay with Chromium's shared per-document native undo stack (verified by probe): interception rules, imperative rewrite on commit, composer behaviour
A three-outcome leave guard (Keep editing / Discard / Save) and one guard inside the ui actions instead of per-entry-point guards; ConfirmDialog API extension
Reload semantics: Save always puts u>=1 in the URL, so a rule is needed for 'URL equals our own snapshot'

Overlay mechanics: mounted inside the page scroll content, pointerover not pointermove, ResizeObserver, hidden during the device width/height animation, scoped to the entering page during AnimatePresence, leaf-only data-edit, no layout change to site elements
Session ownership (site id in the session) and synchronous invalidation on forced world moves (console presets, project change, preview collapsed by drag)
The composer and glow while a session is open (the glow was measured at 4 fps), and dropping `reloading` from the entry gate
A single source of truth for dishes (data/cloud.ts rows versus SitePreview MEALS) and whether meal cards count as static copy or data
Glyph subsetting of typed characters in the published artifact (invisible to check:brief on vite preview)
No-op blur steps and a derived dirty flag
Language semantics of an override on bilingual t() strings
A pixel-diff proof that restructuring SitePreview for editing leaves geometry identical with editing off (the glow test stand and the mini picture)
verdict:
The core state model is right and close to minimal. It adds one per-site world axis, siteEdits, into SITE_AXES, SITE_BASE (TypeScript forces it), DEFAULT_WORLD and the startBuild patch. The session is transient in ui. The write is free, editPlanText-style, with no sendMessage, no credits and no glow. Each Save that changes something counts +1. None of it is in the URL. The rendering and persistence design around it does not hold against the code. BLOCKER: every pinned SitePreview reads the CURRENT site's world (SiteMini.tsx:30,52; SitesShelf.tsx:337,419; Dock.tsx:609; SitePreview.tsx:274-275). Once a second live site exists, the shelf and dock cards show the wrong site's edits, the pick flight pops at landing, and the planned world-only 'no leak' test would pass anyway. MAJOR, from my own probes: (a) a data-URL photo inside World makes every world.set() cost about 40 ms instead of 0.1 ms (1.76 MB world, headless Chromium, 30.09.2026), and hitting the quota silently stops ALL persistence; (b) native ⌘Z crosses editing hosts, including from the chat textarea and from a blurred document, and reverts committed site text behind the store; this refutes 'we don't intercept ⌘Z in chat'. Also MAJOR from the code: (c) ConfirmDialog has only onConfirm, so Save/Discard/Keep editing cannot be built on it as planned; (d) Save always writes u>=1 to the URL, so F5 in preview ALWAYS loses the edits and keeps the counter; (e) the CSS-:hover ring is clipped by the overflow-hidden cards, lights nested editables together, and needs a defined overlay that survives the device animation and page swaps; (f) the content keys don't match the mixed /
/
